title: [20/7/2024] Average annual distance travelled by adults
prompt: The table below gives information about the average annual distance (in miles) travelled by adults and the types of travel in 1997 and 2007. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates the average yearly distance covered by adults using different modes of transport for travelling in 1997 and 2007.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, car, taxi and train travel increased while the remaining means of transport experienced declines. Furthermore, car was the dominant mode of transport in both years, with figures far exceeding all other categories, whereas bicycle and motorcycle consistently recorded the lowest distances covered.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the means of transport that gained popularity, cars dominated in terms of distance travelled, with 3,500 miles covered annually by adults in 1997, significantly higher than train and taxi travel, at 900 and 200 miles in that order. By 2007, the usage of cars for travel doubled to 7,100 miles, remaining the most preferred means of transport at the time. Similarly, taxi journeys saw a four-fold increase to 800 miles, while a modest rise of 100 miles was seen in train travel, reaching 1,000 miles by the end of the period

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining modes of transport, bus travel covered twice the distance of walking in 1997, with respective figures of 800 and 400 miles. However, both saw considerable decreases over the decade, with the former dropping by 300 miles and the latter declining by 100 miles by 2007. Meanwhile, bicycle and motorcycle usage remained consistently low throughout the period, starting at 100 miles each in 1997 before declining slightly to 80 and 90 miles respectively in the final year.
